prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: I keep B056 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The round-1 exchange shows that all eight members describe the same chemical principle: an E3 ligase and a target brought into one ternary complex, followed by catalytic, event-driven removal of the target, confirmed independently across laboratories. That is an enzymatic system turned into a defined reaction that a small molecule directs, and it gives biologists a general tool as well as a modality. The seats beyond Crews and Deshaies should each rest on a distinct, datable discovery. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target meets that test: it explained the mechanism of an already used drug, and it is the entry point for the CRBN-recruiting degraders that make up most of the clinical pipeline. Linke, Sparr and Zou ask whether Ciulli's cooperativity work is the quantitative basis of the field. I value it, but it refines and quantifies a mechanism whose existence the PROTAC concept and the cereblon discovery had already established.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet a broadly approved therapy, and I am recalling trial status without verifying it, so the case rests on mechanism and reproducibility rather than on completed clinical outcomes. A three-name limit leaves out Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim, each with a real claim; Sakamoto as co-author of the 2001 paper and Ito as Handa's co-discoverer of cereblon are the hardest omissions. The PROTAC and glue lineages are also different histories, and a single citation can be read as joining two discoveries.

responses.point: Linke prefers Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli because PROTAC design is a transferable principle and Ciulli's VHL ligands and cooperativity work made degraders drug-like, and he says he could be persuaded that cereblon was the more decisive original step.
responses.response: I asked in round 1 whether a Ciulli trio leaves the glue strand unrecognised acceptably, and your reply is that the citation can say 'induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases' so both strands fit. My difficulty is that a citation can mention glues, but the person whose discovery explains how glues work would not be named, and a claim in a citation that no laureate stands behind is the weaker position. Handa's result is a target identification, but it is a measured, reproducible and datable one, and it changed how an entire drug class is understood. I would only revisit if the expert report shows that the VHL ligand and ternary-complex framework was developed independently of Crews's laboratory and is a founding step rather than an optimisation.

responses.point: Sparr moved B056 to first place with Ciulli and argues that waiting for an approved degrader would hold the prize hostage to regulatory events, so that twenty-five years of independent reproduction is the relevant maturity.
responses.response: I agree with this and it removes the main maturity worry I had. The citation should rest on the demonstrated mechanism and on reproduction across laboratories, not on drug approvals, and I have kept my wording to the chemistry. I differ on the third seat. You say cooperativity and turnover are what make this chemistry and not pharmacology, and that is true, but those quantities were measured on systems whose existence the 2001 concept and the cereblon discovery had already established. Since you say you would accept Handa if the committee chooses him, the disagreement between us seems narrower than the vote counts suggest.

responses.point: Zou says that taking Handa would displace Ciulli, that the glue strand has a separate history, and that the citation should rest on the chemical concept and structural evidence for ternary complexes.
responses.response: I accept your framing that the structural and ternary-complex evidence is the strength of the field, and I agree with you that the glue strand is a separate history. That is the reason for my position: both origins need a named discoverer if the citation covers both. Cereblon is also where structural evidence enters the glue strand, since it showed how a small molecule reshapes the ligase surface to recruit new substrates. You say you would accept Handa if the committee chooses him; with the four of us who already name him, that would give a majority of six for a Crews, Deshaies, Handa trio.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa because each name rests on one datable discovery, but asks how much of the ternary-complex framework belongs to Ciulli rather than the Crews laboratory and wants the citation worded around mechanism and not therapeutic outcomes.
responses.response: I agree with both points, and my citation names no clinical result. I share the request that the expert report separate Ciulli's independent contribution from the Crews laboratory's VHL work, because that is the evidence that would test my own reasoning on the third seat. Your concern that naming Handa could read as awarding two discoveries is fair. I would answer that both discoveries are cases of the same chemical event, recruitment of an E3 ligase to a new substrate by a small molecule, and the citation says that in one clause.

responses.point: Aili would not split B056 into separate PROTAC and molecular-glue parts unless no unified citation can be agreed, and would accept Ciulli as the third name only for a PROTAC-centred citation.
responses.response: I hold the same line and I did not change my configuration. A single part under the principle of E3 ligase recruitment is more defensible than two parts, which would divide the credit within one field and reduce the number of names available to each strand. I would keep the Ciulli option as the fallback only if the committee decides on a PROTAC-centred citation, and I think that outcome is worse than the unified one.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports show that Ciulli's VHL-ligand and ternary-complex work is a founding step that is independent of the Crews laboratory; that evidence would be the main reason for me to change the third seat.

Whether Ito should share the cereblon credit with Handa, and whether Sakamoto's role in the 2001 paper should weigh more than the committee has allowed; I am relying on recollection of the chronology and not on verified records.
Whether the clinical status of degraders, which I recall but have not verified, undermines the argument; I treat it as secondary to the reproduced mechanism.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal. My research on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is not on degraders or any shortlisted candidate, and I have no collaboration or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or the other credited names. I read the round-1 conflict disclosures from Zou, Brzezinski, Aqvist and Sparr; none concerns B056 or me.
